Forecast Discussion

High pressure over the central Appalachians will control our weather through Friday. We'll have plenty of sunshine, gradually warming afternoon temperatures and cold overnight temperatures, especially in the valleys. Mountaintops will be noticeably milder than the valleys overnight.

On Saturday, low pressure develops off the GA/FL coast and a cold front is moving our way from the west. The low moves along the coast Sunday and offshore by Monday while the cold front moves through Monday morning.

This scenario keeps us dry as the low is too far away to provide enough moisture for rain and it also robs the cold front of its moisture. The front likely passes through dry. A small percentage of the model guidance is suggesting the coastal low will move further west, increasing our chances for rain so we can't rule out a shower or two Saturday night.

Behind the cold front, temperatures drop back to near average values.
